title: Zumwalt's store
_about: A counter across the middle of the room. Customers on this side, everything worth having on the other. The counter costs two to climb, and people notice.
_honesty: That Adam Zumwalt's place faced the plaza is documented; the floor plan is period-typical reconstruction. Zumwalt's was actually TWO buildings — a residence and a separate attached kitchen that did duty as a restaurant and boarding house — and this map is only the store side. The shelf stock is taken from a real Texas store advertisement: coffee, sugar, tea, salt, chocolate, soap, candles, tobacco, letter paper, crackers, dried apples, hats, shoes and cheap cotton cloth, plus powder, lead, flints and nails. Not the Madeira and Bologna sausage — that was a Brazos port town's stock, not a frontier village's.

landmarks.label: THE COUNTER
landmarks.note: Everything this town has bought on credit is written in the book lying on it.

landmarks.label: THE SHELVES
landmarks.note: Coffee, calico, candles, nails. The two things a family saves for are a bolt of cloth and a paper of nails.

landmarks.label: THE FIRE
landmarks.note: The clerk's side of the room, and the warm side.

landmarks.label: THE FLOOR
landmarks.note: Where the town stands, argues, and finds out what the government wants.

features.label: Zumwalt's ledger
features.note: Who owes what, and to whom. Nobody in this room is comfortable about it.

features.label: Behind the counter
features.note: The powder keg, the bars of lead, and the salt. Where a customer cannot reach.
